records.Concise description: Blockstream's fully open-source hardware-signer family for Bitcoin and Liquid, now centered on Jade Core and Jade Plus.
records.Deeper researched summary: Jade uses open-source firmware/hardware and a 'virtual Secure Element' design based on encrypted secrets plus Blockstream's blind-oracle/PIN-server architecture rather than a conventional proprietary Secure Element chip. Jade Plus adds a camera and full QR air-gapped workflows, while 2026's Jade Core simplifies the family for ordinary self-custody. Current Jade can work with Blockstream App and third-party coordinators.
records.Launch / history: Original Blockstream Jade launched January 2021; Jade Plus launched January 2025 and Jade Core launched April 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Jade is a major open-source Bitcoin hardware wallet that demonstrates an alternative physical-security design to conventional Secure Element-centric signers and integrates Bitcoin with Liquid.
Important technical or cultural characte: Hardware signing for Bitcoin and Liquid
Jade Plus camera and air-gapped QR PSBT support
Jade Core and Jade Plus consolidated as one family
records.Verification basis: Current Blockstream Jade product/help material and 2021–2026 launch history verify active family, QR/stateless capabilities and open-source security model.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not call Jade's design a conventional hardware Secure Element; Blockstream explicitly uses a different virtual-Secure-Element/blind-oracle model.
QR air-gap capabilities differ by Jade model; Jade Plus has the camera while Jade Core is simplified.
Do not say Jade stores bitcoin; it secures/signs with keys.

records.Concise description: An open-source DIY Bitcoin signer that uses commodity Raspberry Pi hardware, QR codes and a stateless operating model to support single-signature and multisig transactions.
records.Deeper researched summary: SeedSigner is software and build guidance for creating an offline Bitcoin signing device from readily available parts. A typical signer loads a seed only for the active session, exchanges wallet/PSBT data through QR codes and is designed to operate without persistent private-key storage. Current releases support modern script types, reproducible images and extensive internationalization.
records.Launch / history: SeedSigner emerged around 2020–2021 and developed through community releases. Version 0.8.7 shipped in July 2026 with continued active contributions.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It lowered the cost of air-gapped multisig signing and established a popular 'stateless signer' model that does not depend on buying a proprietary hardware appliance.
Important technical or cultural characte: Taproot signing/address support in current lineage
records.Verification basis: Current official site and July 2026 release history verify active development, stateless design, QR/PSBT workflows and project leadership.
Research notes / uncertainties: A DIY device's security depends on hardware sourcing, build process, software verification and operational practice; do not present 'air-gapped' as an automatic security rating.
SeedSigner is a signing device/system, not a wallet that stores bitcoin.

records.Concise description: Open-source Bitcoin signing-device firmware for inexpensive camera-equipped hardware, emphasizing air-gapped QR workflows, descriptors, multisig and Miniscript.
records.Deeper researched summary: Krux turns supported commodity embedded devices into offline Bitcoin signers. It supports QR-based wallet/PSBT exchange, descriptor loading, multisig and advanced policy verification. Releases in March and April 2026 added new hardware targets, descriptor improvements and security hardening; earlier 2025 work added Taproot and WSH Miniscript support.
records.Launch / history: Krux developed in the early 2020s and remains actively maintained; versions 26.03.0 and 26.04.0 shipped in March and April 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It broadens the DIY signer ecosystem beyond Raspberry Pi and is technically notable for current Miniscript/descriptor support on inexpensive air-gapped hardware.
records.Verification basis: Current official repository and 2026 releases verify active status, supported signer model and descriptor/Miniscript functionality.
Research notes / uncertainties: Supported commodity hardware differs in physical properties and supply-chain assumptions; Krux should not receive a generic hardware security rating.
Krux is signer firmware/system, not a device that stores bitcoin.
Krux operates on private-key/seed material to sign transactions; it does not store bitcoin itself.

records.Concise description: Block's seedless 2-of-3 self-custody Bitcoin system combining a mobile app, dedicated hardware key and a Block-managed server key.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bitkey is an integrated Bitcoin wallet rather than a standalone generic signer. Three keys participate in a 2-of-3 policy: one in the mobile app, one in the Bitkey hardware device and one managed by Block. Users control two keys and can move funds without Block, while Block's single server key cannot move funds on its own; it supports recovery and pre-authorized convenience transactions. Recovery uses encrypted backups and delayed/recovery-contact mechanisms instead of a user-managed seed phrase.
Creators / founders: Lindsey Grossman — public Bitkey business lead at launch
records.Launch / history: Bitkey launched globally in December 2023 and remained an active Block product through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is a distinct hardware-wallet architecture that replaces the conventional single hardware key + seed phrase model with a distributed 2-of-3 system and built-in recovery services.
Important technical or cultural characte: Block cannot spend with its single key
records.Verification basis: Current Bitkey recovery documentation and Block's launch architecture verify the 2-of-3 key split, Block's non-unilateral role and integrated hardware/app design.
Research notes / uncertainties: Use precise quorum wording instead of simply saying 'non-custodial': Block holds a server key but lacks a unilateral spending quorum.
Bitkey is intentionally consolidated as one integrated wallet/hardware system; do not split the app, hardware and server key into separate profiles.
Do not say the hardware stores bitcoin; it stores/protects a signing key.
